articles.title: Parties in BARMM polls told to uphold peace amid violence
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Political parties participating in the first ever parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao (Barmm) on Monday were told to uphold peace and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Political parties participating in the first ever parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao (Barmm) on Monday were told to uphold peace and ensure that the right to vote is respected following several reports of violence during the polling.

Among those who reminded parties and stakeholders was Vice President Sara Duterte, noting that the Barmm elections symbolize a historic step for the region towards self-governance, peace and inclusive development.
“Panawagan natin sa lahat ng kandidato, partido, at stakeholder na panatilihin ang isang mapayapa, maaasahan, at transparent na proseso ng halalan,” Duterte said in a statement.
(We call on all candidates, parties, and stakeholders to maintain a peaceful, reliable, and transparent election process.)

“Hinihikayat namin ang mga mamamayan ng Barmm na gamitin nang responsable ang kanilang karapatang bumoto at pumili ng mga lider na tunay na maglilingkod para sa mabuting pamamahala at kapakanan ng Bangsamoro,” she added.
(We encourage the people of Barmm to responsibly exercise their right to vote and elect leaders who will truly serve for the good governance and welfare of the Bangsamoro.)
Katungod Bangsamoro, a consortium of civil society organizations also appealed to political parties to do the same, especially after reports of violence in Cotabato City.

“The heightened militarized presence in the area risks sparking further violence that could frustrate the will of the peoples of the Bangsamoro,” Katungod Bangsamoro Co-Convener Carlos Isagani Zarate said in a separate statement.

“We urge party leaders to act with restraint and responsibility, and to remind their followers that [it is] not senseless violence and bloodshed [that] must decide the future of the region,” he added.
He likewise reminded parties that the elections marked a “historic first” for Barmm, hence it should not be undermined by intimidation, force or fear.
“We call on all stakeholders to protect the integrity of the process and to ensure that the voices of the people are heard and respected,” Zarate said.
Three people were killed during a shooting incident in front of a voting center in Barangay Bagua 2, Cotabato City on Sunday evening, while 15 others were injured.
Two separate explosions were also reported in the same city the same night, injuring at least one individual.

Meanwhile, four people, including a police officer, were wounded in a shooting incident inside Central Pilot Elementary School along Sinsuat Avenue in Poblacion 6, Cotabato City right before regular voting hours started on Monday morning. /jpv

articles.title: Blast heard outside polling center in BARMM-SGA town
articles.summary: MALIDAGAO, BARMM-SGA — A blast believed to be from a grenade was heard outside the compound of the Nabundas Elementary School in Barangay Nabundas of Malidagao town in the Special Geographic…

blocks.text: MALIDAGAO, BARMM-SGA — A blast believed to be from a grenade was heard outside the compound of the Nabundas Elementary School in Barangay Nabundas of Malidagao town in the Special Geographic Area of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) at 11:25 a.m. on Monday.
The explosion happened as throngs of voters were waiting in line for their chance to cast ballots in the first-ever regional parliamentary elections.
Some people left the queue, but they did not go outside the polling area, saying they believed the explosion was only meant to scare them.
The voting, however, was temporarily stopped pending clearance from the military and the police.
By past noon, voting had resumed at the Nabundas precincts./coa

articles.title: BARMM elections: 98.14% of polling centers start voting — PNP
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A total of 1,164 out of the 1,186 voting centers, or 98.14 percent, in the first Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections were now open as…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A total of 1,164 out of the 1,186 voting centers, or 98.14 percent, in the first Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections were now open as of 11 a.m. on Monday, according to the Philippine National Police (PNP).
In a press briefing in Camp Crame, PNP public information chief Col. Allen Rae Co noted that only 22 polling centers in Basilan had yet to begin voting as of this writing.
The PNP is still validating for what reasons voting had yet to start in the 22 remaining centers, Co added.
He further noted that it was “premature” to conclude that the areas in which voting centers had yet to open would indicate a failure of elections.
“It’s too early to tell,” Co stressed.
Some 2.39 million voters in BARMM are set to troop to voting centers across the region to vote for 80 seats in its regional parliamentary.
While regular voting was expected to begin at 7 a.m., some areas reported delays.
Earlier, the PNP said 1,045 of the 1,186 voting centers in BARMM had opened as of 8 a.m.

It also previously noted earlier pronouncements that the Commission on Elections (Comelec) had taken control of Cotabato City following a purported explosion and a shooting incident; and Maluso town in Basilan after reports of allegedly pre-shaded ballots. /jpv

articles.summary: Only a month before its exit, the private equity giant had been seeking to increase its First Gen stake and take the Lopez-led power company private, but the proposal was rejected

blocks.text: Raphael Reyes/Rappler; First Gen images

items: KKR has sold its entire 19.9% stake in First Gen Corporation for approximately P25.77 billion, following a failed attempt to increase its investment.
The shares were sold to Angsana Finance Limited at P36 per share, which is higher than KKR's previous tender offer price of P35.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Global private equity investment giant KKR has exited First Gen Corporation, selling its entire 19.9% stake in the Lopez-led power company for about P25.77 billion, just weeks after an attempt to increase its investment and take First Gen private fell through.

In a regulatory filing, KKR-linked Valorous Asia Holdings said it disposed of 715.8 million First Gen shares on September 10 for P25.77 billion, equivalent to P36 per share. Valorous said the transaction included shares held indirectly through Philippines Clean Energy Holding Inc. and left it with no remaining stake in First Gen.

The buyer was Angsana Finance Limited, which separately disclosed that it had acquired the same 715.86 million shares, equivalent to 19.9% of First Gen’s outstanding common shares. Angsana is incorporated in the Cayman Islands and is wholly owned by Gateway Holdings Limited, the parent of emerging markets investment firm Gateway Partners. Gateway, which operates out of Singapore and Dubai, is already an investor in the Philippines as one of the backers of UNO Digital Bank.
Only a month earlier, KKR had sought to increase its stake in First Gen.

In August, First Philippine Holdings (FPH), First Gen’s parent company, rejected KKR’s non-binding proposal to purchase another 8.43% of the power company from FPH and launch a voluntary tender offer for First Gen’s entire public float at P35 per share. FPH said the proposed price did not represent First Gen’s “true value.”
Had the proposal pushed through, the tender offer would also have supported a potential voluntary delisting of First Gen from the Philippine Stock Exchange.
Now, KKR has instead sold its existing shares at P36 apiece, P1 higher than its proposed tender price.
The exit was also followed by a change in First Gen’s board. Manolo Michael de Guzman resigned as a director and member of the Board Risk Oversight Committee effective September 11.

De Guzman is a senior adviser at KKR and president of Philippines Clean Energy Holding Inc., one of the vehicles through which KKR held its First Gen stake. His resignation came a day after KKR sold its entire stake, although First Gen did not state a reason for his departure. – Rappler.com

articles.title: How Philippine creators leverage AI on CapCut
articles.summary: I just got back from CapCut World Singapore, the first-ever event of its kind. It was a gathering of creators and industry stakeholders who all have one thing in common: they create, edit, and some…

blocks.text: I just got back from CapCut World Singapore, the first-ever event of its kind. It was a gathering of creators and industry stakeholders who all have one thing in common: they create, edit, and some even make money using CapCut. The Singapore leg is CapCut World’s first stop, with two more destinations set for the United States and the United Kingdom.

At the conference, I was able to sit down and talk to creators, agency owners, and academics – an unlikely gathering of kindred spirits who shared their thoughts on AI use, the future of creation, and what really defines art in this day and age.
Grounded on the fundamentals

At the theoretical end of the spectrum, I met Yolec Homecillo—an educator of 15 years in the animation program at De La Salle College of Saint Benilde. I say theoretical because he is formally trained in the arts. But he is also a comic book author and CapCut effect creator behind assets like “seamless blur” and “ink bleed.” He advocates for a theory-first approach: Homecillo emphasizes that creators must ground themselves in classical cinematography, composition theory, and foundational art principles before navigating modern vertical or new media formats.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Tech.INQ (@tech.inq)

For Homecillo, AI is fundamentally a technological tool that streamlines workflows, whereas art is defined strictly by the creator’s personal process and subjective human experience (phenomenology). Consequently, he refrains from using AI in his original artworks. He encourages emerging creators to exercise discernment by separating commercial work (where tools fulfill business efficiency demands) from personal artistic fulfillment (where human identity must be preserved).
AI as a “me” multiplier

On the other side, independent filmmakers like Vee Camallere view AI as a democratic equalizer for narrative expression. AI functions as a workflow accelerator. By adopting tools such as Edit Pilot, Camallere transitions from time-intensive manual editing to streamlined content creation.

There is an insight that traditional filmmaking often excludes talented creators due to substantial budget and equipment constraints. AI allows creation to begin simply with “just one idea”. By conversing with an AI agent, a creator can expand even a 5-second prompt into a complete visual short film, enabling independent storytellers to share their narratives with global audiences. In her presentation, she was able to showcase a workflow where AI helped her build a storyboard, script, setting, and 3D models for her characters that can persist in a serialized drama.

Van Allen Aliparo aka “Aliparongbukid”, another creator who represented the Philippines at CapCut World in Singapore, never dreamed he could collaborate with big brands and foreign artists who made use of his templates when he went full-time as a template creator. CapCut has become more than just an editing tool, but a global platform where over 400,000 templates are created every day. These templates can be used by anyone in the platform – such as Aliparongbukid’s ‘Dilaw’ template that was used by local artist Maki and helped push downloads.

blocks.caption: Van Allen Aliparo aka “Aliparongbukid” and Vee Camallere at CapCut World Singapore

blocks.text: The road forward for creativity

Ultimately, Philippine creators demonstrate that AI on CapCut serves neither as a total replacement for human skill nor as a mere novelty. Whether used to accelerate commercial templates, democratize film production, or highlight the importance of classical art theory, AI functions best as an enhancing co-pilot. By combining foundational principles with active technological research, creators can leverage AI’s efficiency while keeping human story and process at the center of their work.

At CapCut World Singapore, parent company Bytedance announced the debut of the TikTok Awards for local and regional creators will be coming soon. They also announced upcoming new AI features that will be available on the CapCut platform for both free and paid tiers.

articles.title: Alleged ID theft, lax verification reported in Lanao Sur polls
articles.summary: MARANTAO, Lanao del Sur — What was hailed as a historic milestone for the Bangsamoro peace process faced serious integrity questions here on Monday after voters in Lanao del Sur discovered that…

blocks.text: MARANTAO, Lanao del Sur — What was hailed as a historic milestone for the Bangsamoro peace process faced serious integrity questions here on Monday after voters in Lanao del Sur discovered that unknown individuals had cast their ballots.

Mindanao State University (MSU) History Professor Tirmizy Abdullah called the parliamentary election a “milestone in the Bangsamoro peace process” after casting his vote at Bacong Elementary School just before 9:50 a.m.
While Abdullah noted the voting process — from finding his name to feeding his ballot into the Vote Counting Machine (VCM) — was smooth, he pointed out early logistical hiccups.
He said crowd control protocols were not followed, making it difficult and chaotic to enter the school.

He also shared a lighthearted moment, noting that personnel mistakenly applied the indelible ink to his thumb instead of his index finger — which he joked was preferable anyway so it wouldn’t interfere with him picking his nose.
However, Abdullah’s optimism was overshadowed by alleged serious electoral irregularities that his own family experienced.

“Although I was able to cast my vote, I cannot help but feel deeply frustrated and concerned because some of my close relatives were not able to exercise their right to vote,” Abdullah told the Inquirer.
When his relatives arrived at their precincts, they were barred from voting because someone else had signed their names on the master list.

“This situation is deeply troubling because every registered voter should be given the opportunity to personally exercise their right to vote, subject to proper verification,” Abdullah said, emphasizing that the incidents raise serious concerns about the integrity of the voting process.

Abdullah said his cousin, Sitte Rocaya A. Guro, an MSU Law student and registered voter of Precinct No. 5-A, arrived at the Daana-Ingud Bacong Elementary School Voting Center around 9:00 a.m., but was turned away after finding her name already signed on the masterlist.
Guro told Abdullah that poll workers distributed ballots without verifying voter photographs and failed to collect thumb marks, violating standard election procedures.
To prevent further disenfranchisement and ensure accountability, Abdullah urged election authorities to allow local and international observers directly inside the polling precincts.
Currently, observers are only permitted to monitor from the outside.

Abdullah argued that allowing them inside to witness the voting and verification process is vital to “ensure transparency, accountability, and confidence in the integrity of the electoral process.”/coa

articles.title: PPCRV flags multiple voting at BARMM precinct in Maguindanao del Norte
articles.summary: Several individuals were seen casting multiple ballots on behalf of other voters at Central Oring Elementary School in Buldon, Maguindanao del Norte, during the first Bangsamoro parliamentary…

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 12:24pm

Several individuals were seen casting ballots on behalf of other voters at Central Oring Elementary School in Buldon, Maguindanao del Norte, during the first Bangsamoro parliamentary elections, the Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting (PPCRV) reported Monday.
During a press briefing, PPCRV spokesperson Ana Singson pointed out that voting on behalf of another person is strictly prohibited unless authorized by the Commission on Elections (Comelec).
“It is strictly forbidden to vote for another person unless the voter is a PWD who requires assistance and has been authorized by Comelec,” Singson said.
“You cannot vote for your sibling, aunt, uncle, or even your closest friend. You must cast your ballot yourself.,” she added.
PPCRV also reported the distribution of prohibited sample ballots at the school.
Singson cautioned BARMM voters that the campaign period had already ended, making the distribution of election materials strictly prohibited.
“It is also strictly prohibited to bring out or distribute election materials inside the polling precinct. The campaign period is over; it is now election day. So please, follow the rules,” she said.
GMA News Online reached out the Commission on Elections for their comment and will update this story once a response is received.
Gunshots in Lanao del Sur
In other parts of BARMM, PPCRV reported that gunshots were heard at Dilausan Central Elementary School in Lumbaca-Unayan, Lanao del Sur, at around 10:31 a.m.
Singson said people at the school were reportedly running around amid the chaos at the Barangay Dimapaok precinct.
“Update: There were gunshots, and voters were running at the Barangay Dimapaok Precinct,” the report read.
This is a developing story.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: In updated NDC, PH promises to cut more carbon emissions on its own
articles.summary: From 2.1%, the Philippines' has increased its unconditional net emissions reduction to 7%

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 12:18pm

The Philippines has finally updated its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the United Nations, recommitting 75% emissions reduction and adjusting its unconditional emissions reduction targets from 2.1% to 7%. The remaining 68% are conditional.
Unconditional targets are emissions reduction the country plans to do on its own, while the remaining 68% conditional reduction targets remain reliant on international support.
NDCs are climate pledges that parties to the 2015 Paris Agreement need to submit to the United Nations every five years.

While the Philippines' latest NDC came late (countries were scheduled to submit in 2025), its increased unconditional commitment of 7% is regarded as a "massive improvement" among onlookers and experts.

"This is not only a welcomed sign in implementing more solutions to mitigate emissions, but also as a sign of commitment to accountable and good governance," Aksyon Klima Pilipinas (AKP) said in a statement.

According to the 2026 NDC, the emissions reduction covers energy, transport, agriculture, waste, and forestry and other land use sectors, as well as industrial processes and product use, reflecting "an economy-wide scope in determining overall addition and consistency with national greenhouse gas inventory arrangements."

But while the 2026 NDC "trends in the right direction," AKP highlights the pertinent fact that "our country’s capacity to implement its own solutions have been depleted in recent years by corruption, as evidenced by the flood control scandals."

"Through this lens, a higher unconditional target also means there must be higher allocations in the 2027 national budget and beyond to ensure proper implementation of identified NDC solutions – from nature-based solutions (NbS) to improved energy efficiency and conservation," it said.

Meanwhile, Gerry Arances, Executive Director of the Center for Energy, Ecology, and Development sounded the alarm "that the Philippine government’s nationally determined contributions (NDC) do not include a concrete commitment to phase out fossil fuels."

"This is a severe misalignment not only from international commitments to mitigate global temperature rise below 1.5℃, but also from the government’s duty to ensure the climate survival of Filipinos," he continued, adding how the latest report from the United Nations Environment Programme said the world is set to overshoot the 1.5C goal with best case scenarios now pegged at 1.8C.

"With the transition away from fossils being non-negotiable to combating the climate crisis, the government’s lack of firm commitment to phase out fossil fuels signals less than minimal efforts to protect our communities and to contribute to the global struggle," Arances said.
But in the 2026 NDC, the country admitted adaptation, instead of mitigation, remains its priority, as it only has a "minimal contribution to global GHG emissions."
According to Our World in Data, the Philippines emitted a total of 175 million tonnes of CO2 in 2024 — or just some 0.45% of the world's CO2 emissions of the same year.
It's paltry compared to China's 12.3B, or Europe's 4.88B.

In its statement, AKP echoes Arances and CEED, saying a missing element "from the 2026 NDC is a decarbonization pathway aligned with the long-term goal of the Paris Agreement to limit warming to 1.5°C."

"Having this pathway is the benchmark with which we assess the implementation of the nation’s climate strategies - not just the NDC, but also in other areas of climate work, such as carbon markets and just transition," it added.
Says AKP, "stating the pursuit of 'low-carbon development" is impossible "without leaving fossil fuels behind."

Sustina co-founder Anna Reyes goes back to the ratio of 7% unconditional against 68% condition and says it is a little mind-boggling. "I don’t know how to read that as anything other than a decision to do the minimum domestically and frame the rest as someone else’s responsibility." — GMA News

articles.title: Rise in abuse of election candidates is ‘changing politics’ in England
articles.summary:
Electoral Commission finds abuse, particularly of women, minority ethnic and disabled people, is affecting candidates’ behaviour

Abuse and intimidation of election candidates is “a serious…

blocks.text: Abuse and intimidation of election candidates is “a serious and growing concern”, the Electoral Commission has said, as a review of this year’s local and mayoral elections in England revealed a surge in threats to those who stood.
More than half of the candidates for Labour or Reform UK reported abuse while those most likely to be targeted were women, people from minority ethnic backgrounds and those with disabilities.

A report by the commission said candidates described being spat at and verbally and physically assaulted. It found that levels of abuse had reached the point where it was changing the behaviour of people standing in elections.

“I had to take my husband out on the door this time, which was a first,” said one candidate, who was among a third of those who said they may not stand for election again because of harassment or intimidation.
They added: “I felt quite independent previously, but there was so much anger from men of an older age at the door and some younger men, all disillusioned by politics and let down.

“I did understand that, but it was the anger and insults and close confrontation at times which was so aggressive. I feel I have to protect myself in public and not be on my own, for the first time in local politics, and will never put myself in any vulnerable places on my own again.”

Female candidates were more likely to change their behaviour over such concerns. More than three-quarters (79%) said they avoided campaigning on their own at least once, compared with 46% of male candidates, while 57% avoided speaking on controversial topics, compared with 32% of men.

Vijay Rangarajan, the chief executive of the Electoral Commission, said: “Our single biggest worry now is this rise in abuse and intimidation. It’s not directed at any one party and there seems to be a variety of causes.”
He said there was an increasing trend towards the “othering” of political opponents, “literally, a dehumanisation” and a blurring of the boundaries of civility, in some cases driven by social media.

“I think we’re going to see a kind of complete blurring of the online and offline worlds,” he said. “We’ve seen people in the real world walk down the street filming someone to produce an online video. And then when others see that online video, they get very angry and they go and start following someone else down the streets. So this kind of real, complete interaction between online and offline is a real feature.”

Rangarajan said he was struck by two particular cases. One was a disabled candidate who said they were threatened on the doorstep but “couldn’t run away” because of their disability. Another was a candidate who was targeted on social media and whose daughter called from school to say she had seen the online abuse and people were calling her parent a racist, fascist and Nazi.
after newsletter promotion

The commission made a number of recommendations, including calling on social media companies to do more to tackle the online abuse of candidates by developing rapid response protocols, and calling on parties to urge their members to respect other campaigners.

The review found 59% of Reform UK and 54% of Labour candidates told of personally experiencing inappropriate behaviour, harassment or threats to their security, followed by 42% of Greens, 37% of independents, 26% of Tories and 22% of Liberal Democrats.
Rangarajan said the changes made by some candidates in how they campaigned was affecting local politics.

“It takes away, in some cases, things like meeting your candidate, which is really important in our politics. The second thing is it definitely affects women much more and ethnic minority candidates too, and even more if you’re both. People are stopping wanting to be candidates because of this and that’s a real problem,” he said.
Rangarajan called for a “multi-partisan approach” from parties.

“We’re all up for really robust debate, that’s what the whole election is about and it wouldn’t work if it wasn’t … but it’s got to have a modicum of respect to it as well and there are some things which are really unacceptable, like following someone’s family down the street, for example, trying to video them, or posting people death threats.”

On the upside, the report found that voters continue to be satisfied with how elections are run, with 94% of voters in England expressing satisfaction with the voting process, similar to 2025 (95%) and the last comparable elections in 2022 (96%).

Nevertheless, voters remain concerned about the accuracy of election information. More than half of those surveyed said they had seen misinformation, and one in 10 said they had seen deepfake material.

Rangarajan welcomed proposals in the representation of the people bill to protect election agents’ home addresses, extend protections to electoral staff and increase sentencing for offenders against candidates, elected officials and electoral staff.

articles.title: [Rappler’s Best] A vote buried in the noise
articles.summary: You can’t be blamed for having lost track of the crucial events that led to today’s BARMM elections — because Manila continues to dominate the attention economy with the antics and shenanigans of…

blocks.text: The first of its kind parliamentary elections in the Philippines are finally happening today, Monday, September 14, in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), after repeated postponements in the last four years.
Something hopeful is happening in the country, and it’s happening in BARMM, was how civil society groups put it in this curtain-raiser by Iya Gozum. We’re covering the polls live here.

The late former president Noynoy Aquino must be wincing in irony, he who paved the way for this historic vote when he shook hands with the rebel commander Ebrahim Murad and signed a peace deal with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in 2012. After all, it’s under the son of the dictator who fueled the Mindanao rebellion that these elections are now taking place.

The Aquinos have had a soft spot for the MILF. Nearly a year after she was catapulted to power in the 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution, then-president Corazon Aquino met in Cotabato City with the unarmed Murad, who gave her a bouquet of flowers tied with a yellow ribbon. I recalled that moment, and what happened (or did not happen) after, in this piece.

items: Murad and the MILF have controlled the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) that was set up in 2019 after the “yes” vote won in the Bangsamoro plebiscite. The BTA was meant to prepare the region — its bureaucracy, its people — for self-governance and today’s historic polls. What has the BTA accomplished? Watch here.

Yet, the MILF found itself repeating the mistakes of its predecessor in the region, the Moro National Liberation Front, as its leaders squabbled over funds, appointments, and Malacañang’s interference.
In March 2025, what had been brewing happened: a leadership shake-up ousted Murad as BTA chief minister and put in place the Marcos administration’s bet, Abdulraof Macacua.

blocks.text: Today, Murad and the MILF fight for survival and relevance through the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), which is fielding the most number of candidates for district, party, and sectoral seats at 81. Macacua’s Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) is not far behind with 74 candidates.

items: Violence persists, with the region still hobbled by persistent threats from extremists, as pointed out by Reemar Alonsagay in this piece.
How can the next BARMM government make sure no one’s left behind? Shay Du lays out the challenges and opportunities in this report.

blocks.text: Our reporters Iya Gozum and John Sitchon, who are in Cotabato City, covered the colorful grand rallies of the political parties last Saturday, September 12, (watch their report). While an important political process, the polls have been clouded with uncertainty and fear, Herbie Gomez wrote in this story.

items: These elections are unique for at least five reasons, as explained by Shay Du in this story.
Over 600 candidates are vying for just 80 seats — 70% of whom are men and 38% of whom belong to Gen X. Here are the other numbers that matter.
In this story, John Sitchon and Shay Du introduce us to the dynasts, elites, and power blocs competing for the polls. What parties are running? Check them out here.

blocks.text: You can’t be blamed, though, for having lost track of the crucial events that led to today’s elections — because Manila continues to dominate the attention economy with the antics and shenanigans of politicians based here.

Former speaker and presidential cousin Martin Romualdez was charged with plunder on September 7, a non-bailable offense, but, quick to the draw, he had himself confined in Cardinal Santos hospital before he could be served an arrest warrant.

items: Jairo Bolledo walks us through a bizarre timeline of events that led us to yet another Saturday spectacle (after Sara Duterte’s dramatic court entrance the previous Saturday) of authorities moving Romualdez from Cardinal Santos to the Philippine General Hospital, which is now the Sandiganbayan’s refuge for “independent” medical examination of high-profile public officials facing prison.
Jairo shows us in this report how to delay detention, Romualdez edition.

blocks.text: While Romualdez and his counsels are now in uncharted legal territory, the judiciary handed the other side of the Marcos clan an astounding victory: the Supreme Court reversed a previous court ruling that convicted the President’s 97-year-old mother, former first lady Imelda Marcos, of graft in 2018 — and acquitted her.

items: This adds to the list of record-high wins for Marcos family members and their cronies accused of corruption under the Marcos dictatorship.

In Mrs. Marcos’ latest victory, what was overturned was the Sandiganbayan’s ruling that she had taken part in the management of Swiss foundations that were set up with public funds amounting to $200 million. The SC’s 1st Division said the evidence against her was not properly authenticated, among other reasons cited for the acquittal. Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda wrote the decision that was concurred in by associate justices Ramon Paul Hernando, Henri Jean Paul Inting, Ricardo Rosario, and Jose Midas Marquez.

blocks.text: By the way, Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo is retiring in November. The Court in August opened applications for the post.
We take this moment to express our condolences to the family of the revered sports journalist Recah Trinidad, who died on Sunday, September 13.

Val Villanueva takes a deep dive into documents pertaining to Villar Land’s revaluation and recognition of enormous accounting gains. Read Part 1 here and Part 2 here.

articles.title: Historic BARMM vote opens under shadow of killings, ballot tampering
articles.summary: Comelec has taken control of Cotabato, Maluso as BARMM voting opens.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 11:59am

MANILA, Philippines — Voters across the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao began casting ballots Monday, September 14, in the region's first parliamentary elections, as violence and reports of election irregularities disrupted voting in several areas.
At least three people were killed and 15 others wounded in Cotabato City hours before polls opened, while authorities also reported gunfire, an explosion and alleged pre-shaded ballots in Basilan.

The Commission on Elections later placed Cotabato City and Maluso, Basilan under Comelec control, giving the poll body direct authority over local officials, government employees and law enforcement to address security threats and protect the integrity of the vote.
More than two million voters are eligible to elect 80 members of the first regular Bangsamoro Parliament, marking a major step in a peace process that established BARMM after decades of conflict.
In Marawi City, voters formed long lines outside polling stations early Monday as soldiers, police personnel and armored vehicles stood guard, Agence France-Presse reported.
"We're excited, we came here early in the morning," 18-year-old voter Mohammad Actar Macabada told AFP after casting his ballot.
"I'm nervous because there might be chaos. Before there was chaos. Now it's peaceful," he said. "I'm excited for the results."
More than 20,000 security personnel have been deployed across BARMM, with quick response teams placed on standby.
Explosion near polling area
An explosion, meanwhile, also reported Sunday evening in MB Kalanganan, Cotabato City.
Police said a male resident of Poblacion 1 was injured after he saw a bright light and heard a blast while waiting for his construction foreman.
Comelec Chairman George Garcia said the Philippine National Police later determined that the blast involved an improvised explosive device.
AFP separately reported that a man died in hospital early Monday following an explosion near another polling station. Police were still investigating its cause.
The incidents were among those cited by Comelec in placing Cotabato City under its control.
"Just earlier, the Commission en banc decided to place Cotabato City under Comelec control," Garcia said.

Placing an area under Comelec control gives the poll body direct supervision over government officials and law enforcement involved in the election. The declaration also allows it to direct security deployments and other measures needed to protect the vote.
Pre-shaded ballots in Basilan
Comelec also placed Maluso, Basilan under its control after authorities discovered that ballots in 36 of the municipality's 68 precincts had allegedly been pre-shaded overnight.
"We determined as of last night that the ballots in 36 of the 68 precincts had been compromised. We found that all of them had been pre-shaded," Garcia said in mixed English and Filipino.
(Left) Election officers prepare the vote counting machines in a classroom in a voting precinct. (Right) A pre-shaded ballot discovered by the Comelec in Maluso, Basilan.
Commission on Elections / Released
Garcia said election officials had identified those believed responsible and ordered the reprinting of ballots for the affected precincts.
Several ballot boxes also had broken seals, although Garcia said a closer inspection found that the ballots inside other boxes remained intact.
Voting continued as scheduled in Maluso's remaining 32 precincts.

The PPCRV separately reported "rampant" vote buying in Barangays Marang and Gadung in Barira, Maguindanao del Norte, as well as reports of voters casting ballots multiple times at Central Oring Elementary School in Buldon.

As of Monday morning, all clustered precincts in Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Tawi-Tawi and the Special Geographic Area had opened, while 81.46% of clustered precincts in Basilan were operational.
The Bangsamoro polls are the culmination of a decades-long peace process that led to the creation of BARMM and the transition from an appointed interim government to an elected parliament.
Deadly Cotabato shooting

Violence also marked the hours in the leadup the Monday's vote. Before midnight on Sunday, gunfire broke out outside Datu Usman Mampen Elementary School in Cotabato City after supporters of rival political groups jostled for position in a queue ahead of voting.
Cotabato police chief Jibin Bongcayao told AFP that the confrontation began as a struggle over who would vote first.
"It started as a struggle for position in the queue between two groups," Bongcayao said.
"It led to shoving, escalated into a fistfight, and eventually gunfire broke out in a crowded area."
Police confirmed that three men were killed, including an 88-year-old resident, while 15 others were wounded and taken to hospitals.
Scene-of-the-crime operatives recovered shell casings believed to have come from .45-caliber and 9mm firearms.
Bongcayao said those involved belonged to rival political parties that emerged from the Moro Islamic Liberation Front.
Separate gunfire was also reported Monday at Dilausan Elementary School in Lumbaca-Unayan, Lanao del Sur, according to the Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting.
Media reports also cited gunfire at Central Pilot School in Cotabato City, prompting the deployment of Philippine Marines and police. — with Agence France-Presse

articles.title: [EDITORIAL] Pinagpala talaga si Imelda Marcos at Martin Romualdez
articles.summary: 'Victory for impunity' raw ito sa ilalim ng sistema na laging talo ang accountability kapag bumangga sa kapangyarihan, yaman, at pagde-delay gamit ang legal muscle

blocks.text: 'Victory for impunity' raw ito sa ilalim ng sistema na laging talo ang accountability kapag bumangga sa kapangyarihan, yaman, at pagde-delay gamit ang legal muscle
In a way, it was a good week for the Marcoses and Romualdezes — napawalang-sala si dating first lady Imelda Marcos mula sa pitong counts of graft.

With every intention of sounding sarcastic, we’re quoting Imelda herself, “God is love. I have loved. Therefore, I will go to heaven.” Nabilaukan man kayo o hindi, tandaan ninyo ang sense of entitlement sa pahayag na ito that only Imelda can deliver.

Ito namang si dating House speaker Martin Romualdez, sinusuwerte pa rin kahit hinahabol ng Ombudsman, dahil sa oras na inilabas ang arrest warrant niya para sa 7.44-billion plunder case, bigla siyang naospital. ‘Yan ba ang klase ng suwerte na galing sa bilyon-bilyong yaman?

Anong larawan ang ipinipinta nito? “Victory for impunity,” sabi ng analysts at advocates. Ito ang sistema kung saan laging talo ang accountability kapag bumangga sa kapangyarihan, yaman, at pagde-delay gamit ang legal muscle.

Mabilis ring nabasa ni Rappler investigative head Chay Hofileña at ng kanyang team ang template, “Top officials, including past presidents charged with plunder and/or graft and corruption, suddenly fell ill or developed illnesses that merited confinement.” (BASAHIN: Romualdez joins list of officials who cite illness to delay custody)

Ipagpalagay na natin na talagang may sakit ang mga opisyal na ito. Sabi ni Southern Illinois University criminology associate professor Raymund Narag, ipinapakita nito na “selectively available to the rich and powerful” ang medical considerations. Kung mahirap ka at may kondisyong pangkalusugan, makatatambay ka ba sa ospital kahit may arrest warrant?

This is a graphic story of how power, privilege, and family shield the elite. Konektado ang dalawang kaso sa nakaupo ngayon sa Malacañang. Imelda Marcos is the mother of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Martin Romualdez is his first cousin.

Despite the fallout between Marcos Jr. and his cousin, talaga bang walang kinalaman ang pagiging Romualdez niya sa desisyong pagbigyan siyang manatili sa Cardinal Santos at pagkatapos ay ipa-test pa sa University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital? Gagawin ba nila ito para sa lahat ng magdadahilan na hindi sila puwedeng ikulong dahil may sakit?
Mabalik naman tayo kay Mrs. Marcos. Sabi ng human rights lawyer na si Ruben Carranza, ipinapakita ng acquittal ni Imelda Marcos ang “long-standing problems in the Philippine justice system.”

Ano’t ano man ang naging hatol ng mga korte, hindi nito binabago ang true historical narrative: ang human rights violations noong Martial Law, ang civil forfeiture rulings, at ang mga nabawi ng estado at ng mga biktima na ill-gotten wealth.
Sabi ng representante ng ACT Teachers Party-List, ipinapakita ng acquittal na tila hindi kayang ikulong ng justice system ang “biggest plunderers.”
Hindi maihihiwalay ang magkasunod na dagok ng impunity na ito sa Marcos legacy.

Ngayong nagbabanggaan ang dalawang legacy sa buhay ni Marcos Jr. — ang “mahiya naman kayo (shame on you)” SONA speech na nag-trigger sa flood control corruption exposés at ang baluktot na pamana ng Martial Law — ano ang gagawin ng Pangulo?

Pero kung nais in Marcos na ipamukha sa mundo na hindi niya kinukunsinti ang pinsan at labas siya sa mga kalokohan ng kanyang dating most trusted lieutenant — dapat niyang seryosohin ang pagpapataw ng patas na batas.

Kapag ang batas ay istrikto sa mahihirap, pero nababaluktot para sa presidential relatives — hindi lamang ‘yan suwerte. ‘Yan ang kaibahan ng langit at lupa ng mayaman at mahirap. That is impunity, that is injustice. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Who is ex-Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang?
articles.summary: Former Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang on Monday took the witness stand in Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial.

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 11:44am
Former Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang on Monday took the witness stand in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.
During direct examination by prosecutor Chel Diokno, Cabotaje-Tang said she graduated from the San Beda College of Law in 1979.
After passing the Bar Examinations and taking her oath in 1980, Cabotaje-Tang joined the Supreme Court as a judicial assistant, a position she held for two years.
She then moved to the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG), where she worked for almost 31 years and handled more than 1,000 cases by her estimate.
Following her stint at the OSG, Cabotaje-Tang was appointed associate justice of the Sandiganbayan, the country's anti-graft court.
She later served as Sandiganbayan presiding justice from 2013 to 2024.
According to Cabotaje-Tang, the presiding justice is the primus inter pares, or “first among equals.”
“But in terms of formal rank, we are all equal, except that the presiding justice does some administrative work and leads the cour,” she said.
Cabotaje-Tang retired from the Sandiganbayan in 2024.
She currently teaches Criminal Law at San Beda University and the University of Santo Tomas.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: LPG group asks gov't to suspend excise tax on fuel products
articles.summary: With fuel nearing P100, an oil company and transport groups press government to suspend taxes.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 11:35am
A store helper selling Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) changes the LPG prices on their price board in Paco, Manila on March 25, 2026.
STAR / Edd Gumban
MANILA, Philippines — LPG company REGASCO urged the government to temporarily suspend excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and other fuel products as Dubai crude oil prices remained elevated.

REGASCO and LPG Marketers Association President Arnel Ty said Dubai crude prices are currently above $100 per barrel, prompting the group to write Energy Secretary Sharon Garin to appeal for the suspension of excise taxes.

"Sabi namin, kami po'y umaapela na pupuwede na po siyang magrekomenda sa Department of Finance na suspendihin na po hindi lang [ang excise tax] sa LPG at kerosene, kasama na po ang diesel, gasoline," Ty told dzMM in an interview Monday, September 14.
(We are appealing for her to recommend the suspension of excise taxes not only on LPG and kerosene, but also on diesel and gasoline.)
Ty said if their request for an excise tax suspension is granted, LPG prices may go down by P3 per kilogram, diesel by P6 per liter, gasoline by P10 per liter and kerosene by P5 per liter.
Another round of oil price hikes is expected to take effect Tuesday, September 15, as global oil prices continue to rise due to conflicts affecting the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz.
The latest projected increases could push some fuel products beyond P100 per liter at certain stations.

Under Section 148 of the National Internal Revenue Code, as amended by Republic Act 12316, the president may suspend or reduce excise taxes on petroleum products upon the recommendation of the Development Budget Coordination Committee, in coordination with the Department of Energy, when the one-month average Dubai crude oil price reaches or exceeds $80 per barrel.
Dubai crude is one of the major oil benchmarks used in Asia and influences local fuel pricing.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. exercised the authority earlier this year when he issued Executive Order No. 114 in April, suspending excise taxes on LPG and kerosene for up to three months.
As local fuel prices are expected to rise further this week, transport group MANIBELA launched a two-day transport strike from Monday until Tuesday, September 15.
MANIBELA criticized Secretary Garin's earlier remarks that the government has limited control over local fuel prices because the Philippines imports most of its oil supply.
"For transport workers, however, saying that there is little the government can do is not enough while fuel prices continue to rise and directly eat into their daily income," MANIBELA said.

"I ⁠think ​he's behaved reasonably well, and we ​behave reasonably well," the US president said.
Trump's remarks follow a pattern set by his administration, which has sought to downplay tensions with China, despite frustration in Washington over Beijing's support for Iran.
Trump has previously warned China not to provide Iran with weapons. The US sanctioned three Chinese satellite companies in May for working with Iranian military entities.

articles.title: Alan Jones told prominent athlete ‘I would like to be kissing you all night’ after alleged assault, trial hears
articles.summary:
Alleged victim tells court he froze and was ‘in disbelief’ after broadcaster kissed him on corner of his lips at public event

A prominent athlete froze and was “shocked and embarrassed” when…

blocks.text: A prominent athlete froze and was “shocked and embarrassed” when Alan Jones kissed him on the side of his mouth at a public event, the broadcaster’s trial at Sydney’s Downing Centre has heard.

The witness said the kiss on the corner of his lips happened years after Jones sent him a weekly bouquet of flowers after he had complimented the flowers on Jones’s dining table. He said Jones’s driver would drop the flowers at his home every week.

The court is hearing the first day of evidence from the third alleged victim of Jones, known as complainant M, whose case involves two of the 22 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching against Jones.
Jones has pleaded not guilty to all charges.
The athlete said Jones kissed him on the corner of his mouth as he walked across a large event room to get back to his table.
He didn’t say anything at the time, he said. “I was shocked and embarrassed and I knew I did not want to be there,” he said.

“I’m not certain, but I think I froze at that time,” he said. “I was in disbelief of where this was happening, and I didn’t understand why it was happening, and there’s no reason to suggest why in this public situation you’d kiss someone this way.”
After the dinner, Jones texted M saying something like “I would like to be kissing you all night”, the witness said.
Asked by prosecutor Georgina Wright SC if he consented to being kissed this way, he answered no.

The athlete testified that he was interviewed by the 2GB broadcaster on multiple occasions as a teenage athlete, later developing a friendship which included visiting his apartment at Macquarie Street in Circular Quay for meals.
He said Jones was always introduced him in an “incredibly overwhelmingly complimentary” and “flattering way”, which made me him feel “awkward and uncomfortable in how glowing it was”.
He said Jones would welcome him with a hug and a kiss on the cheek and use flattering terms like “champion” and “beautiful man”.
The court heard Jones texted the alleged victim with words to the effect: “If someone hasn’t told you, let me be the person who tells you that you’re special.”
The witness said it was flattering at first but then it “got uncomfortable” because not even his parents talked to him that way.
The first time he had a meal at the apartment he complimented the tableware and he later received a set of the same tableware from the broadcaster.
The witness said on one visit to Jones’s Fitzroy Falls farm with his room mate, he broke down and cried when telling Jones about his financial difficulties.
The broadcaster offered to help and organised a meeting at Jones’s apartment – known as the Toaster – between the bank, his agent and his accountant.
The trial continues.

articles.title: [Newspoint] Lorna Kapunan for the people
articles.summary: Known through all her nearly half-century of practice as a terror at litigation, she looks in perfect form

blocks.text: Known through all her nearly half-century of practice as a terror at litigation, she looks in perfect form

items: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has been largely repetitive, with significant evidence of her alleged embezzlement presented during earlier hearings.
Lorna Kapunan, a prominent lawyer, is pushing for Duterte to testify in court, challenging the court's credibility and the defense's lack of substantial arguments.
Duterte's legal team is struggling to defend her, and the court faces pressure to address Kapunan's motion, which poses a moral challenge to their authority.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

But for the excitingly audacious performance of Lorna Kapunan, the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has been little more than a rerun of the hearings that led the House of Representatives to impeach her and send her to trial in the Senate.

I watched those hearings religiously. They were riveting. It was there that the crimes imputed on Duterte — embezzlement of hundreds of millions of taxpayer pesos, among others — were solidified by evidence to such a degree that I thought they did not need further proving. Indeed, I thought a trial would be a mere formality, especially since the regular rigors of judicial adjudication don’t apply — no jail, no restitution, only sacking and a lifelong ban from holding public office.

Also, the accusations went virtually uncontested at the pre-impeachment investigation. Although lawyers were allowed to prompt all those called to it, and although a lawyer herself, Duterte refused to appear. Now at trial, with a battery of lawyers allowed to speak freely for her under more flexible arrangements, she has taken the opportunity only as an even more convenient excuse to be absent.

Anyway, with scarcely anything other than technical arguments to deploy, her lawyers have not been impressive. True, they have yet to present their case in her defense, but what possibly do they have in their arsenal that can turn things around? Lorna Kapunan knows and pushes forward.

Known through all her nearly half-century of practice as a terror at litigation, she looks in perfect form. She looks the part too, in command, as the most senior of the private counsels who have teamed up with members of the House prosecuting the case. And she now forces the issue. She is asking the impeachment court to summon Duterte and have her explain herself in person, in court, on national television and across all online platforms.

Duterte’s chief counsel is quick to come to her rescue and invoke, all too predictably, everyone’s constitutional right against being forced to give testimony that can be used to prove their own guilt. Wedged between a plundered nation and a suspect presumed, as a matter of course, to be inviolably in possession of one of the most basic individual rights, the court chooses to go easy with the latitude granted it by law, which, for one thing, leaves it to make its own rules and render unappealable decisions. Apparently thinking first of dispelling the storm of debate gathering over Kapunan’s motion, the court decides to shelve it.

All that rare excitement provided by Kapunan happened on the 23rd day of trial, when the court last convened, adjourning to reconvene after an unusually long six-day recess that ends today (September 14). But you can be sure Kapunan’s motion will continue to hang ominously over the heads of the senator judges until they realize they have to deal with it, and do so promptly, for their own credibility. Never mind that they have allowed the trial to grow tedious, but allowing Sara Duterte to go off accusing them of “bending the law” against her!

It was only days before Kapunan made her motion that she last made that accusation, and she did it with characteristic theatrics — the “drama queen,” as her own father had described her when once she went so far with her propensity to play victim as to state, publicly, that she herself had been raped.

With her fixtured herd of cheerleaders behind her, she stood outside the office of the regional trial court that had issued a warrant for her arrest on charges of grave threats. She had gone on social media to warn President Marcos, his wife, and his cousin Martin Romualdez, the Speaker at the time, that she had contracted an assassin to kill all three of them. In the end, she posted bail to buy herself provisional freedom, but not before she taunted the police to cuff her and put her behind bars. It would have made a great photo-op for her had the police not wised up to her antics.

In fact, any court or institution of law that attempts to exercise jurisdiction over her gets it. Not even the International Criminal Court has been spared. She accuses it of being “a puppet…a lapdog” of President Marcos, her family’s archenemy.

Her father, Rodrigo, has been in detention in The Hague, the Netherlands, awaiting trial before that court on charges of “crimes against humanity” for the thousands of deaths in the war on drugs during his presidency (2016-2022). Although not an accused herself, she is mentioned in affidavits of confessed assassins for Duterte as complicit in some of those extrajudicial killings.

That’s why the impeachment court cannot just bury Kapunan’s motion in its agenda on some procedural pretext. Her motion is no mere legal request; it constitutes a moral challenge to a court precisely given the singular power to put the likes of Sara Duterte in their place. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Peptide user tore oesophagus after using counterfeit product, Australian regulator warns
articles.summary: TGA issues alert after person was hospitalised after believing they were taking experimental weight loss drug retatrutide

blocks.text: A patient who tore their oesophagus after taking a counterfeit version of an experimental weight loss drug has prompted Australia’s medicines regulator to warn of serious risks of such products.

The concern relates to retatrutide, a type of drug known as a peptide. Retatrutide has not been approved by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) or regulators overseas, and it cannot be legally prescribed or sold in Australia.

Peptides are strings of molecules called amino acids that act as chemical messengers in the body, and are involved in a range of functions like hormone activity, digestion, immune defence, and tissue growth. The peptides in retatrutide mimic hunger hormones.

Despite being unapproved, the drug has been widely promoted on social media and promoted for sale on the hidden market, with names including retatrutide, Reta, R-10 and R-20, and they often come in unmarked vials.

The TGA was alerted after someone experienced such severe and uncontrollable vomiting – after taking what they believed was retatrutide – that they tore their oesophagus, which can be life-threatening. They required treatment in hospital.
The TGA obtained a sample of the product and found it contained a different peptide that also targets hunger, called semaglutide, and no retatrutide.
The amount of semaglutide detected was approximately eight times higher than levels found in approved semaglutide products assessed by the TGA.
The TGA’s chief medical adviser, Prof Robyn Langham, said products being sold online may be fake or counterfeit and could contain ingredients that pose serious risks to health.
after newsletter promotion

“The biggest risks with unapproved peptide products are not knowing what is in the vial, how much of or even what substance it contains, whether it is sterile, or whether it contains other contaminants or toxins,” she said.

“These risks are particularly concerning for injectable products, where contaminated or non-sterile manufacturing can increase the risk of infection and harmful immune responses including anaphylaxis.”
People who self-inject face additional risks such as incorrect dosing, unsafe injection technique and serious adverse reactions, Langham said.
The Victorian health department issued a similar warning in June, after it was notified of six cases of acute liver toxicity associated with products labelled as retatrutide.

The head of the TGA, Prof Anthony Lawler, said imported and illegal products are “not subject to the same controls over the quality or efficacy of the goods when compared with medicines approved for supply in Australia”.

Australia’s chief medical officer has previously issued a public health warning about unapproved and non-prescribed peptides, after reports of serious adverse effects including liver damage, inflammation and severe allergic reactions.

articles.summary: Authorities have rescued 108 people from the ship, which was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan

blocks.text: DISASTER. An aerial view of the Virgo Transport 8 passenger ship that capsized in Indonesia's Java sea, September 13, 2026, in this still image taken from video.
BASARNAS/Handout via REUTERS
Authorities have rescued 108 people from the ship, which was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan

JAKARTA, Indonesia – More than 600 Indonesian rescuers were searching for 129 people still missing after a passenger ship capsized in the Java Sea on the weekend, an official said on Monday, September 14, with the death toll steady at six.

The Virgo Transport 8 ship carrying 243 people went missing in bad weather early on Sunday, the rescue agency said. Authorities have rescued 108 people from the ship, which was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.
“We have continued the search for the missing since early in the morning. We are deploying 622 personnel and around 12 ships,” I Putu Sudayana, head of the Banjarmasin rescue agency, told Reuters.
He said there was no increase in the death toll of six as of Monday morning.
In a video shared by the rescue agency, a large red-and-black ship lies capsized and partially submerged in choppy blue water, with its red-painted underside visible above the surface.
Two small boats, each carrying people, were seen floating near the capsized ship amid rough water.
On Sunday, Edy Prakoso, another official at the national rescue agency, said the ship leaned heavily to one side after strong waves hit its starboard side.
A passing helicopter reported the vessel had capsized, Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said on Sunday, with the cause still being investigated.
Indonesia relies on ferries across its 17,000 islands, where sea travel is cheaper and more accessible than flying, and there have been numerous accidents.

In separate incidents last month, two ferries carrying hundreds of passengers caught fire in waters. Five people died when a ferry caught fire off Madura island, while one person died in a fire on a ferry travelling from the tourist island of Bali. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: The first-ever Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary elections kicked off with early voting hours at the San Vicente Academy in Cotabato City on September 14, 2026. Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairman George Erwin Garcia, accompanied by other Comelec officials, personally toured and observed the proceedings.
Comelec handout
The Comelec decision comes as violence is reported in Cotabato City and pre-shaded ballots are found in Maluso town in Basilan

items: Two areas in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao were placed under Comelec control due to violence and compromised ballots during the first parliamentary polls.
Cotabato City experienced three violent incidents resulting in three deaths and 15 injuries, while Maluso town had pre-shaded ballots in 36 out of 68 precincts.
Comelec Chairman George Garcia announced that despite the issues, voting will continue in unaffected precincts, and new ballots will be reprinted for compromised areas.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Two areas in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao were placed under the control of the Commission on Elections (Comelec) on Monday, September 14, due to reports of violence and compromised ballots as the region holds its first parliamentary polls.
Comelec Chairman George Garcia announced the development in a voting precinct in Cotabato City as early voting started at 5 am.
Garcia said Cotabato City was put under Comelec control because of at least three incidents of violence on Sunday night, September 13, the eve of election day.

blocks.caption: Early violence mars election morning in BARMM regional center

blocks.text: He said that three were dead and 15 people were injured after a confrontation while queuing up to vote resulted in physical violence and shooting at 11:45 pm on Sunday.
In another area, an explosion occurred on Sunday night. The one who set off an improvised explosive device got injured and is currently hospitalized.
Garcia said there was another shooting incident in the city but no one got hurt.
Meanwhile, Maluso town in Basilan was also put under Comelec control as poll officials determined on Sunday night that the ballots in half of the voting precincts were compromised.
“‘Yong 36 of the 68 precincts ng mga balota, nalaman namin na ito ay lahat ay na-preshade. As to sino ang nag-preshade, alam na namin pati mga detalye,” he told reporters.
(We found that the ballots in 36 out of 68 precincts were pre-shaded. We already know who did the pre-shading and other details in the incident.)
Garcia said the Comelec will not declare a failure of election in Maluso town.
He said he immediately ordered the reprinting of ballots for the 36 precincts, with the Comelec telling voters and teachers serving for the elections to wait for the arrival of the new ballots.
For the remaining precincts, voting will continue as Comelec determined the ballots there were not compromised. However, voting in Maluso has been delayed due to the issue.

“Bagamat ilang boxes na naglalaman ng mga balota, ‘yong sealed boxes, ay na-compromise ‘yong seal, pero upon further verification, walang effect as to the integrity of the ballots. Walang napalitan and therefore ‘yan ay magagamit,” Garcia said.

(While the seals of the boxes containing the ballots were compromised, but upon verification, there is no effect to the integrity of the ballots. No ballot was changed, and therefore these ballots can be used.)
He said this was an election offense, with the Comelec was determining if the incident could be classified as a case of electoral sabotage.
More than two million voters are expected to cast their ballots during the historic BARMM parliamentary elections. – Rappler.com

articles.title: PGH: Martin Romualdez not confined in 'presidential suite'
articles.summary: The Philippine General Hospital (PGH) on Monday clarified that Leyte Representative and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez is not confined in a “presidential suite".

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 9:31am
The Philippine General Hospital (PGH) on Monday clarified that Leyte Representative and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez is not confined in a “presidential suite".
PGH spokesperson Dr. Jonas del Rosario said there is no such accommodation at the hospital.
“He is not confined in a presidential suite. Wala po kaming ganoon (We do not have such a room),” Del Rosario said in a message to GMA News.
He also said that Romualdez is not confined in a psychiatry ward.
According to him, the room being used by Romualdez was prepared following the short notice given to the hospital.
The PGH said the room was selected based on several considerations:

items: Will be easy to secure, this being at the end of the corridor and on the 7th floor
Will not disrupt flow of patient services
Big enough to accommodate the required security, equipment and personnel to perform the services and tests needed for example the Dobutamine stress echo test
Only one remaining big private room available as of the time of the court order

blocks.text: "The PGH Director will be appearing at the Sandiganbayan today to disclose the findings in court," Del Rosario said.
Romualdez was transferred to the PGH in Manila from the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City on Saturday morning.

PGH officials were tasked by the Sandiganbayan Third Division with assessing if Romualdez needs medical confinement after an arrest warrant was issued against him. Otherwise, he could be detained at the Quezon City Jail.

Romualdez’s doctors have told the anti-graft court that he needed to remain confined in a medical facility. Some of the illnesses cited by his doctors included a fluctuating blood pressure and the risk of a stroke. —AOL, GMA News

After the inauguration of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao in 2019, its people are finally electing members of their own parliament. For seven years, the President appointed the members of the Bangsamoro Parliament, which has since gone through three terms.
Planning to catch up on poll updates to see who the people will elect?

articles.title: Israeli minister threatens to strip Israeli film-makers of citizenship over Gaza documentary NAZA
articles.summary: Miki Zohar accuses Oscar-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor of ‘treason against the state’

blocks.text: Israel’s culture minister has called for the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of NAZA, a documentary about the country’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, to be stripped of their citizenship, accusing them of “treason against the state”.
NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza.

In the film, the Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor spoke to 24 different Israeli military or intelligence whistleblowers who outlined the AI-powered targeting systems used to bombard Gaza that have killed tens of thousands of civilians. In one interview, a source claims that approval had been given to kill 500 NAZA in order to kill one Hamas member.
The 80-minute documentary won a special jury prize at this year’s Venice film festival on Saturday, after receiving a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record.
On Sunday Israel’s culture minister, Miki Zohar, accused the directors on X of being willing to “harm their homeland in order to receive applause from antisemites around the world”.
“I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for treason against the state,” Zohar wrote on X.
Other Israeli ministers also took aim at the directors, who won an Oscar in 2025 for their film No Other Land about Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank.
“You are a disgrace and an embarrassment to the entire people of Israel. Go away!” the far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, said on X.
“I am certain that your friends, that is to say our enemies Hamas in Gaza, will welcome you with open arms.”

The revocation of nationality is legally possible in Israel, although it is rarely applied. In 2022 the supreme court confirmed that the state may strip people of their nationality if they have failed to show “loyalty”, for example by committing acts of espionage or treason.
The law was also expanded in 2023 to apply to people convicted of “terrorism”.
The law requires the interior minister to submit the revocation request, the justice minister to approve it and judges to validate it.
Abraham’s family home was targeted by a rightwing mob after the world premiere of 2024’s No Other Land, which spotlighted Palestinian resistance in the occupied West Bank.

“We’re taking risks in a system that privileges us, that has Jewish-Israeli supremacy as its founding characteristic,” he told the Guardian, adding: “For so many Palestinians, it’s not a rightwing mob that’s coming to their home: it’s US-funded bulldozers and weapons.
“Imagine if a Palestinian journalist in Gaza tried to do what we did and called up senior Israeli officials. There is no comparison. They would most likely be murdered.”

The Israeli military has responded to NAZA by saying it “categorically rejects” the allegations made in the documentary and criticised the use of anonymous testimonies, saying the identities of the whistleblowers “cannot be verified”.

The Palestinian militant group Hamas launched an attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, which resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an Agence France-Presse tally based on official Israeli figures. Hamas militants also took 251 hostages to Gaza.
The Gaza health ministry has reported more than 73,000 deaths in the subsequent three years of Israeli bombardment, the vast majority of which have been civilian casualties.
– Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title: Motorcyclist’s death reignites debate over potholes on Victoria’s ‘deteriorating’ roads
articles.summary:
Coalition says potholes must be fixed ‘as a matter of urgency’ after 71-year-old crashed and died on the Western Highway at Trawalla, west of Ballarat, on Sunday

Emergency services were…
articles.byline: Australian Associated Press and Benita Kolovos

blocks.text: Emergency services were called to Trawalla, west of Ballarat, shortly before 1pm on Sunday after reports a motorcycle had struck a pothole.
The 71-year-old rider, from Ballarat, died at the scene after reportedly losing control on the Western Highway, near Trawalla Road.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the crash, which are yet to be determined.
But the incident has revived concerns about the quality of Victoria’s public roads, an issue which is shaping up to be a key election flashpoint.
A report from the Victorian auditor general on 9 September found 48% of the network was in poor or very poor condition.
This was up from 39% in 2021.
Examining more than 23,000 kilometres of state roads, it characterised the overall condition of Victoria’s public roads as “deteriorating”.
The Victorian Coalition has pledged $5bn over four years to plug 1m potholes and re-establish preventive road maintenance.
The Labor government, meanwhile, has committed $352m to double the number of potholes fixed in 2026 from 250,000 to 500,000.
In a statement the premier, Ben Carroll, described the incident as “a tragic loss of life” and said “road conditions aren’t good enough”.
“Victoria police have been clear that the circumstances are still under investigation, so I’m not going to pre-empt that,” he said.
Speaking on ABC radio, Carroll said “the buck does stop with us”.

“I’ve made it very clear there cannot be any more buck passing on road maintenance. That’s why I have said, under my government – it was outsourced in the mid-1990s – I’m going to bring road maintenance back inside of government.”

The shadow minister for roads and road safety, Danny O’Brien, said the death was “the saddest possible consequence to have come from the terrible state of Victorian roads and it should never have come to this”.

“These potholes need to be fixed and fixed properly as a matter of urgency. It is time for action and this needs to be the highest priority now so that no more lives are lost on Victorian roads because of government neglect,” he said.
O’Brien said the Liberals and Nationals would continue to press the government to bring forward road maintenance works for regional Victoria’s most dangerous roads.
The Victorian state election is due to be held on 28 November.
